newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mobutu's son says father ready for concessions -TV.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's son says father ready for concessions -TV.

text.p: Zaire's ailing leader Mobutu Sese Soko is ready to make concessions to rebel leader Laurent Kabila in peace talks scheduled for later this week, his son told Belgian RTL-TVI television on Monday.

Asked if Mobutu was ready to relinquish power in favour of a transitional regime led by archbishop Laurent Monsengwo, N'Zenga Mobutu said, "It's too early for me to say that...Everything depends on the negotiations. But the president is ready to make many concessions...serious concessions to end the present crisis."
Kabila, whose ADFL forces control 80 percent of Zaire and are closing in on its capital Kinshasa, was due to meet Mobutu on a South African naval vessel on Wednesday.
The ADFL has, however, already rejected Monsengwo's proposed appointment as a transitional leader. The proposal was made by Mobutu supporters at the weekend.

The rebels' newly appointed diplomatic counsellor to Belgium, Etienne M'Baya, reiterated that opposition in a separate interview with RTL-TVI on Monday at the opening of a ADFL embassy-in-waiting in Brussels.
"Mr Monsengwo cannot play a role in the structure of transition (of power)," M'Baya said. "We don't see how someone who does not represent the...democratic forces can play a role in this phase."
